problem:
Determine if $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?

activity_context.topic_title: The Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalue that Corresponds to a Given Eigenvector
examples.problem: Determine if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14056271/assets/82b99a6e1a271ac0b205a3199b023a582877692c3a61dd4b7144312342fea761.png) is an eigenvector of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14056271/assets/2b9e07d0a0089107dc34bb092167719b6e83a4c41ee9f055949a43549449d65e.png) If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
examples.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $\mathbf{v}$ such that $A\mathbf{v}=\lambda \mathbf{v}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =4v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $A\mathbf{v}=4 \mathbf{v},$ we conclude that $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda=4.$
